core_obligations: Let x_1, ..., x_r be the isolated closed points, viewed as schemes, and form the morphism from the coproduct of the curve components C_1, ..., C_t and the points onto X (proof lines 10082-10088).
Note that this morphism is finite and surjective and that both source and target are proper over k, so ampleness of L is equivalent to ampleness of its pullback (proof lines 10089-10092).
Read the criterion off the degree conditions on each component, completing the proof up to line 10094.
proof_roadmap: Form the coproduct of the components and isolated points.
Use invariance of ampleness under finite surjective morphisms.
Reduce to the degree conditions on the components.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reduces ampleness of an invertible sheaf on a proper reduced scheme of dimension at most one to positivity of the degree on each one-dimensional component and on each isolated point. The proof exhibits the finite surjective morphism from the coproduct of the curve components and the isolated closed points onto X, uses that ampleness is equivalent to ampleness of the pullback along such a morphism, and then reads the criterion off the degree conditions on the components (proof lines 10081-10094). H2: the reduction through the coproduct morphism and the transfer of ampleness along a finite surjective morphism is the substance.
